transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Kim (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramos (Redwood SE), Alan Moreno (Lakeshore CISO), Priya Singh (VP Eng), Ben Carter (IT Ops), Ellen Zhao (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick weekly sync on POC security items: SSO setup, audit logging/retention, SOC2 evidence, KMS/encryption questions, and next steps for pilot data handling. Agreed to run SSO test next week and share SOC2 docs. SE to provide audit-log sample and retention options.

Topics:
- SSO / SAML integration and test accounts
- Audit logs: fields, format, retention and export
- Data retention and redaction for pilot data
- SOC2 evidence and compliance posture
- KMS / encryption at rest and in transit
- RBAC and admin controls + console access

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: okay hello everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Maya from Redwood, i'll do a quick roll call
[00:10] Alan: hey Alan here, CISO at Lakeshore, good to see you
[00:13] Priya: Priya here, VP Eng
[00:15] Ben: Ben from IT ops
[00:17] Jonah: Jonah, SE at Redwood, hi all
[00:20] Maya: cool, quick agenda: SSO status, audit logs, retention, soc2 docs, then questions. we ran through the results from last week's test, and a couple items popped up, mainly around audit log granularity and retention windows

[02:05] Alan: yeah on SSO side we tried the SAML metadata you sent, got a bit stuck on the nameid format, our IdP defaulted to email but the session wasn't mapping to the right user in the console, maybe attribute mapping?
[02:35] Sofia: ah right yeah we saw that in the dev logs, the console expects a uid claim by default but we can accept email, it's configurable on the SSO side. i'll drop the mapping doc.

[03:12] Priya: can you confirm whether SSO will provision roles automatically or we have to do manual RBAC mapping?
[03:25] Jonah: short answer: we support SCIM for provisioning and SAML for auth; RBAC mapping can be automatic if you include the groups claim, otherwise we can map groups to roles on our end. for the pilot you can do manual assignment, but SCIM is available if you want automated provisioning.

[06:00] Ben: on audit logs, we need to be able to pull raw logs for the pilot window, with timestamps, user, action, resource, and IP. can Redwood export in JSONL or does it only ship to cloud logging?
[06:25] Jonah: we can stream logs to your target (splunk/elk/stackdriver) or provide S3 exports; logs are JSON lines with fields: ts, user, action, model, route, tokens, client_ip, request_id. i'll attach a redacted sample.

[07:40] Ellen: retention - we need a 90 day retention for pilot artifacts but anything longer has to be archivable. what's Redwood's default?
[07:58] Maya: default hosted retention is 30 days for request payloads, 90 days for metadata; but for dedicated/private we can configure retention longer. during pilot, we can set a 90 day retention for logs and 30 for payloads with redaction.

[09:05] Alan: and encryption? does it use customer-managed keys for dedicated/private?
[09:15] Jonah: yes for Private and Dedicated we support KMS integration and bring-your-own keys (BYOK) for at-rest encryption; hosted uses provider-managed keys but we offer envelope encryption and TLS in transit. we can provide the KMS integration guide.

[11:30] Priya: SOC2 evidence - we need a summary of controls and a redacted report to present to our auditors, what can you share?
[11:47] Maya: we have a SOC2 Type II report and a security controls deck; we'll send a redacted report and summary. full report can be shared under an NDA if needed. i'll add that to the action items.

[13:20] Ben: just clarifying: when you say 'redact', are logs redacted automatically or we need to do application-side redaction?
[13:36] Jonah: we can do either; we provide configurable redaction rules server-side for PII tokens, and you can also strip or pseudonymize before sending. for the pilot we recommend server-side redaction plus a data-retention policy.

[15:02] Alan: about audit exports, would it be possible to get a daily batch export to our S3 with encryption using our KMS key?
[15:18] Jonah: yes daily S3 export with SSE-KMS using your key is supported for Dedicated/Private; for hosted we can forward to a customer bucket with provider-side encryption - we'll confirm exact options.

[17:45] Priya: network/configuration question: we need VPC peering or a private link for traffic to avoid egress through public internet during pilot. which is supported?
[18:05] Sofia: VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink are supported on Private deployments; for Dedicated we can set up VPC peering with controlled egress. we'll capture network diagrams in the deep-dive.

[20:10] Maya: i want to call out one item from last week's tuning run: we saw some KV cache misses causing higher token usage in one workflow; SE suggested adjusting prefix caching and batching. Jonah, do you want to go over that briefly?
[20:30] Jonah: yeah quick note — the KV cache warmup on that workload was low because of short-lived sessions; we suggested increasing session affinity and enabling prefix caching for repeated prompts. that dropped token cost ~18% in our test. for production you'd want a longer-lived Redis-backed cache or configure request affinity.

[22:50] Ben: any compliance concerns with caching model outputs? e.g., are we storing user PII in cache?
[23:05] Jonah: caches can be configured to strip sensitive fields and respect retention; we also support token-level hashing to avoid storing raw PII. will include config examples.

[25:40] Ellen: just flagging data residency - pilot data must reside in US-east only. can you confirm region controls?
[25:52] Maya: yes region pinning is available for Dedicated and Private; hosted can be regionally pinned within supported regions. we'll confirm the region for the pilot and lock it down.

[27:30] Alan: on the legal/procurement side, we might need to see standard data processing addendum and a list of subprocessors. can you provide that?
[27:45] Maya: yes DPA and subprocessors list will be sent. note that some hosted features require subprocessors in cloud infra, we'll annotate those.

[29:00] Priya: timeline question - if we finish SSO and log export tests next week, are we ready to start the next phase of the pilot (load test)?
[29:20] Jonah: yes assume SSO + audit export validated then SE can run the load test with realistic fixtures; timeline depends on network setup and sample data availability.

[31:10] Maya: ok let's confirm concrete next steps: Maya to send SOC2 and security deck; Jonah to send audit log sample and retention config; Alan to share IdP metadata and test user; Priya to provide retention policy; schedule deep-dive for VPC/KMS.

[33:30] Alan: sounds good, one quick question - how do you handle access revocation if a contractor needs to be removed immediately?
[33:45] Jonah: immediate deprovision is supported via SCIM or manual revocation in the console; tokens and sessions can be invalidated centrally. we'll include the revoke flow in the doc.

[36:10] Ben: about cost vs latency tradeoffs we talked about earlier — any recommended guardrails for the pilot to limit spending while getting reasonable latency?
[36:30] Maya: yes we recommended rate limits, model variant fallback, and batching policies; for the pilot set a lower QPS limit and enable automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model for non-critical routes. SE can provide suggested knobs.

[38:25] Priya: can we get a short checklist of what the prod-security handoff will look like? auditors want to know what will change from pilot to prod.
[38:40] Maya: we'll produce a prod-security handoff checklist: SSO/SCIM, KMS/BYOK setup, audit log retention, data retention/archival plan, subprocessors list, SOC2 evidence, penetration test reports if applicable.

[40:00] Ellen: last item from compliance: are you able to provide sample audit entries that show redaction applied so auditors can see PII removed?
[40:12] Jonah: yes we'll produce redacted and raw (redacted fields) examples and a short explanation of redaction rules.

[42:00] Maya: ok wrapping up, thanks everyone. i'll send the SOC2 summary and deck by Monday, Jonah will send logs sample and retention options by Thursday, Alan will share SSO metadata by Friday. we'll plan the technical deep-dive for next week. any other questions?
[42:25] Alan: none from me, thanks
[42:30] Priya: all good
[42:35] Ben: thanks
[42:38] Jonah: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links
[44:00] Maya: meeting adjourned, thanks

References / shared artifacts mentioned:
